metric_units: balanced accuracy, AUROC, Cohen's kappa, shares and the arms' means are proportions in [0,1]; estimate_pp and interval_95_pp are percentage points of balanced accuracy (x minus y); log_r is the natural log of R; log loss is in nats per window; step_time_s and batch_time_s are seconds, indicative; counts of people, windows, parameters and multiply-accumulates are whole numbers
scope: Route 2 of the decision-research roadmap: shared encoders with fixed heads, question-conditioned heads and independent models at matched data and compute, on motor imagery (OpenBMI) and sleep (BOAS), with EESM19 as a crude replication. Every figure compares set-ups; none is a deployment error rate, and nothing is ranked where intervals overlap. Every BOAS figure travels with the three stated gaps and the attribution in boas_conditions.

one-representation.title: One representation, several questions: shared encoders, fixed heads and question-conditioned heads

design.questions_asked_by: Every question is a label-backed classification target from one dataset, asked by identifier: a learned 16-dimensional embedding of the question's index, never language.

levels.E1: EEGNet trained from scratch in its published configuration; the shared trunk has 2,096 parameters on motor imagery and 1,200 on sleep. Three seeds. Primary.
levels.L1: Frozen CBraMod features with the heads trained on top. Three seeds. Primary.
levels.E2: CBraMod adapted by LoRA (rank 4) together with the heads. One seed. Secondary; on sleep it ran after every other result was known (owner decision, 7 October 2026).

arms.B-lin: One shared encoder with one linear head per question: the fixed heads.
arms.B-sh: One shared encoder, one shared hidden layer (width 66 on E1 motor imagery by the ±10% parameter rule, 64 elsewhere) and one output per question.
arms.C1: B-sh plus FiLM conditioning from the question's 16-dimensional embedding: the question-conditioned head.
arms.-fz: The same head on frozen CBraMod features; B-lin-fz-sgd trains the linear heads by SGD.

design.matching: B-lin, B-sh and C1 share initialisation, batch order and step count, see the same windows and labels and run one encoder pass per window. A trains one encoder per question; that cost is what sharing saves, and the ledger counts it.
design.folds: Five person-disjoint outer folds per dataset (all sessions or nights of a person in one fold); no validation set, no early stopping; the final epoch is scored.
design.metric: Balanced accuracy averaged per person, then equally over people. It compares set-ups and is not a deployment error rate. P3 and S4 compare AUROC through log R, R = (1 - AUROC of the dedicated model) / (1 - AUROC of the read-out).
design.single_seed: A one-seed entry resamples people only and carries no training-run variance.
design.canary: Before any fit, a ridge classifier on each window's per-channel mean and log-variance, trained and tested within the first fold's training people only. A question it answers at a balanced accuracy of 0.85 or more is demoted: reported, never counted. No question was demoted.
design.headroom_gate: A question's entries count for a route sentence only if the 95% interval of the level's fixed-head (B-lin) arm lies above chance + 5 pp and below 95%; otherwise they are reported and labelled floor or ceiling. For P3 only the floor applies: the read-out's AUROC interval must lie above 0.55.
design.freeze: The protocol was frozen on 2026-10-06 at 07:17 UTC and amended eight times for engineering only (A1-A8) before the first stage-1 fit at 09:24 UTC; delta, the P3 cut, the canary and the gates are identical in every version. Outer-test labels were masked until scoring. Nothing was selected on test results; no fit failed and nothing was re-run.

margin.fixed: by the owner on 2026-10-06, at the freeze, before any pilot result

flags.difference: yes when the paired 95% interval excludes 0, with its direction (e.g. 'C1 higher'); otherwise 'no difference shown'
flags.margin: 'equivalent within delta' when the whole interval lies inside (-delta, +delta); otherwise 'non-inferior' when the relevant bound alone meets the margin (P1, P4, P5: upper bound of conditioned - fixed below delta; P2: lower bound of shared - independent above -delta; P3: lower bound of log R above log 0.8); otherwise 'margin not met'
flags.independence: The two flags are computed separately and both are always printed. An interval such as [+0.4, +1.6] pp is 'difference: C1 higher' and 'equivalent within delta'; [-3, -1] pp is 'difference: B-lin higher' and 'non-inferior'.
flags.inconclusive: an entry with 'no difference shown' and 'margin not met' is worded 'inconclusive at this sample size'

margin_bound.upper: P1, P4, P5 and their analogues: the upper bound of the more complex arm minus the simpler one below +delta
margin_bound.lower: P2, S10 and S12: the lower bound of shared minus independent above -delta
margin_bound.log_r: P3 and S4: the lower bound of log R above log 0.8

design.route_sentence_rule: stated for a domain only if (a) at least one primary question of the domain passes the canary and the headroom gate; (b) every such question has P1 margin flag 'non-inferior' or 'equivalent within delta'; (c) the ledger rule makes B-lin 'for less' than C1. The sentence must name any question where P1's difference flag is 'C1 higher', with its interval, and list the questions excluded by the gates.
design.uncertainty: Hierarchical paired bootstrap: 2,000 draws, seed 20261006; people with replacement, then seed indices per outer fold; percentile 95% intervals. Single-seed entries resample people only and carry no training-run variance.
design.multiplicity: 21 pre-declared primary entries (P1 5, P2 5, P3 1, P4 5, P5 5), no correction, each with both flags; at 95% about one in 20 null entries may show a 'difference' by chance, which every write-up states. The route sentence uses an all-questions rule (intersection), which does not inflate its error. Everything else is secondary, exploratory or descriptive and labelled so.

It ran with temporary private resume checkpoints (owner decision 2026-10-07), each deleted when its fit completed.

rights.privacyReview: Released on OpenNeuro under CC0 by its authors (ds005555, version 1.1.3). The dataset description states approval by the Comité de Ética de la Investigación de la Comunidad Autónoma de Aragón (C.I. PI24/046). The README states that participants, adult members of the general population, provided written informed consent. Neither says whether the consent covered public sharing. Both statements come from the publisher's dataset description and README; no peer-reviewed paper describes BOAS. The ethics reference was added in version 1.1.1 (May 2025) with no approval date. Published here: cohort-level participant-equal means with person-level bootstrap intervals, paired contrasts with their intervals and per-seed points, log R with its interval, cohort-level AUROC, log loss and Cohen's kappa, cohort-level stage counts and question prevalences, the share of test windows where two heads disagree, and the canary's cohort-level balanced accuracy on the first fold's 80 training people; every cell pools at least 20 people (the smallest, 71). No per-person, per-night or per-fold value, no per-person percentiles, no identifier, date or demographic. Only the polysomnography EEG and the human-consensus labels are used.

protocol: The questions are label-backed classification targets from one dataset each, asked by identifier. They are not language prompts and say nothing about unseen questions (route 3).
MI-A also separates a cue display and position in the run from imagery; MI-B is offline trials only; MI-C and MI-D are about the recording context, not brain states.
SL-B, SL-C and SL-D are deterministic functions of the 5-stage label. Results on them are about head design, not about new information in the signal.
SL-F is time of night, correlated with stage; SL-E concerns the next 30 s, not a prediction horizon in general.

With identifier-only conditioning, FiLM can differ from the same head without it only by per-question thresholds and signs of the shared hidden units. A null result does not show that language conditioning cannot help.

At E1 the shared encoder is a small CNN whose trunk has 1,200-2,096 parameters; P2 there is 'small-CNN trunk sharing', not foundation-model sharing; E2 on motor imagery ran at one seed, as a secondary arm.
SL-E and SL-F are largely predictable from the current stage; their results are shown beside a stage-only readout.
Questions answerable from window statistics or at floor or ceiling are reported but do not count for the route sentence.
Costs were measured on a shared GPU and are indicative; parameter counts, encoder passes and multiply-accumulates are exact.
Three datasets (EESM19 as a crude replication), one lab each, and one fixed recipe per encoder: this is not a ranking of encoders or of multi-task methods.
BOAS has natural stage prevalence but is one population and one PSG system; balanced accuracy across people is not a deployment error rate.
boundaries.secondary: secondary; single-seed arms do not represent training-run variance; EESM19 and S13 crude (20 people)
added: Per-person balanced accuracy averages people equally; it compares arms and is not a deployment error rate.
The OpenBMI numbers here use route 2's own 2-s windows, label-free high-pass and person-disjoint folds; they are not comparable with the site's OpenBMI cross-session calibration figures.
EESM19 full (S13) uses every stored epoch that passes the published core rules at its natural stage mix; it is a different protocol from the site's balanced sleep-scalp subset.

On EESM19 (S13) no stage-only readout was computed (S11 is defined on BOAS only), so its SL-E and SL-F entries must carry the sentence that both questions are largely predictable from the current stage.
E2 sleep ran after every other result was known; its design and run condition were fixed at the freeze, and nothing about it was chosen from results.

not_published: Per-window predictions and probabilities, features, adapted weights and the temporary resume checkpoints, fold assignments, and per-person, per-night, per-recording or per-fold values of any kind.

The per-person 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of the OpenBMI contrasts that the release candidate carries, as the OpenBMI release of 3 October 2026 dropped its own; the BOAS ones never left the private run root.
The BOAS stage-0 pilot standard deviations of per-person paired differences: a per-person spread.
Any BOAS cell of fewer than 20 people, demographics, recording dates and clock times, nights per person, and any hypnogram, epoch or trace from a real recording.

Measured compute time: GPU-hours used, wall time per fit and per block, and training steps per outer fold. The cost ledger publishes its exact items and, labelled indicative, the two times measured interleaved across arms on a shared GPU; the E2-sleep disclosure keeps its run condition, a stage-0 projection of at most 6 GPU-hours.

The text of the audits' discrepancy lists, which names private files and machines. The four items that must travel with the results are carried: the multiplicity statement, S2 at Level 1 labelled as computed by the audit, a gate label on every secondary entry, and the E2-sleep disclosure.
The per-recording metadata behind the third BOAS gap: only the release facts are stated (the ethics reference added in version 1.1.1, no approval date).
The release candidate's generated headline sentences and the handoff's prose: the pages write their own copy from the values.

The handoff, the release candidate, the aggregates, the protocol, the BOAS rights review and the three independent audits: pinned by SHA-256 in this manifest and checked, never copied, because they carry private storage paths.
